import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 730

*References:*
  - [erdosproblems.com/730](https://www.erdosproblems.com/730)
  - [A129515](https://oeis.org/A129515)
-/
namespace Erdos730

abbrev S :=
  {(n, m) : ℕ × ℕ | n < m ∧ n.centralBinom.primeFactors = m.centralBinom.primeFactors}


/--
Are there infinitely many pairs of integers $n < m$ such that $\binom{2n}{n}$
and $\binom{2m}{m}$ have the same set of prime divisors?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_730 : answer(sorry) ↔ S.Infinite := by
  sorry

/--
For example, $(87,88)$ and $(607,608)$ are such pairs.
-/
@[category textbook, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_730.variants.explicit_pairs :
    {(87, 88), (607, 608)} ⊆ S := by
  rintro _ (rfl | rfl) <;> exact ⟨by decide, by native_decide⟩

/--
There are examples where $(n, m) ∈ S$ with $m ≠ n + 1$.

(Found by AlphaProof, although it was implicit already in [A129515])
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_730.variants.delta_ne_one : ∃ (n m : ℕ), (n, m) ∈ S ∧ m ≠ n + 1 := by
  dsimp [S]
  use 10003
  use 10005
  norm_num [Finset.ext_iff, Nat.choose_eq_zero_iff, Nat.centralBinom]
  simp_rw [Nat.choose_eq_descFactorial_div_factorial]
  intro p hp
  constructor
  all_goals exact fun h' => or_self_iff.1 (hp.dvd_mul.1 (
    h'.trans (by refine' of_decide_eq_true (by constructor : _ = ↑_))))


end Erdos730

status_issues.source_status: The current Erdős Problems page records an affirmative solution by GPT Pro, prompted by Price. The linked manuscript is dated June 24, 2026, and proves the stronger assertion that infinitely many consecutive central binomial coefficients have the same prime divisors.
status_issues.evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/latex/730 says: “This was solved ... by GPT Pro (prompted by Price),” and records ≫ x^(1/2) qualifying adjacent pairs with n ≤ x. Theorem 1.1 of https://www.overleaf.com/read/gpttrsmhbhbk#a7cfdf concludes: “there are infinitely many consecutive pairs of central binomial coefficients having the same set of prime divisors.”
status_issues.suggested_change: Change the category to research solved, replace answer(sorry) with answer(True), and cite the linked solution. No change to S or the mathematical condition is needed.

reformulations.difference: The source asks for infinitely many pairs with n ≠ m; Lean counts only pairs with n < m.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Equality of prime-divisor sets is symmetric. If D denotes the source's set of distinct-index pairs, then D = S ∪ Prod.swap '' S. Thus S infinite implies D infinite, while S finite implies D finite. A sorry-free proof of the equivalence, also expanding prime-factor equality into the source's pointwise prime-divisibility condition, compiled in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

review.notes: Checked S and all three theorems. Nat.centralBinom is exactly binomial(2n,n) and is always positive, so primeFactors' exceptional value at zero is unreachable. Allowing the index n = 0 adds no pairs: its coefficient is 1, whereas every positive-index coefficient is even. These facts and the positive-index reformulation were proved in the scratch file without sorry. Lean evaluation confirmed (87,88), (607,608), and the nonconsecutive witness (10003,10005), as well as the source's triple (10003,10004,10005). The existing delta_ne_one proof has no sorryAx; explicit_pairs uses native_decide as written. All declarations faithfully state their intended mathematics; the only issue found is stale status.
